top_stories.title: AWS IAM announces Access Troubleshooter to debug access denied errors
top_stories.summary: AWS IAM has launched Access Troubleshooter, a new feature that provides full authorization context behind access denied errors to eliminate trial-and-error debugging. The tool gives developers and administrators visibility into the complete authorization decision chain within AWS IAM.

top_stories.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
top_stories.summary: Huntress researchers analyzed three phishing kits—EvilTokens, Knight Office, and Kali365—that capture and replay Microsoft 365 session tokens to bypass authentication. The kits target M365 session cookies to hijack authenticated sessions, circumventing MFA protections, with researchers providing detection and containment guidance.

top_stories.title: Fraudsters feed the right face into identity checks through virtual cameras
top_stories.summary: Entrust's 2027 Identity Fraud Report reveals document fraud remains the largest attack category in identity verification, though rates fell 19% year over year. Physical counterfeits comprised 61.1% of fraudulent document submissions, while attackers are exploiting virtual cameras to inject manipulated facial images into identity verification checks.

top_stories.title: Linx Security extends identity governance to AI agent actions
top_stories.summary: Linx Security announced four new capabilities extending identity governance to AI agent actions, including Shadow AI Agent Detection and Agent Runtime Control. The release also includes Autopilots for governed agentic workflows and a Prompt-to-Workflow feature that converts plain-English descriptions into tested agentic workflows.

top_stories.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
top_stories.summary: Threat actors compromised Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI package, publishing malicious versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 that execute a credential stealer on every Python start. The compromise was identified by multiple security vendors including Aikido, Chainguard, Wiz, and others, with the malicious versions published 33 minutes apart on November 17, 2026.

news.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
news.summary: Russian cyber espionage group COLD RELIC (formerly COLDRIVER/UNC4057) used stolen Google Workspace data from one compromised U.S. organization to breach a second organization. The attack chain demonstrates credential and identity data harvested from cloud environments being weaponized for lateral movement into third-party targets.

news.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
news.summary: A Java vulnerability dubbed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) enables pre-authentication remote code execution in widely used applications including Keycloak, Jira, and Jenkins. The flaw exists in Java 17.0.6 and later versions, but is limited to x86-64 Intel and AMD processors supporting the AVX-512 VBMI instruction set.

news.title: Cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds
news.summary: Attackers are stealing cloud credentials and access secrets exposed in public Docker Hub images within as little as eight seconds of publication. The findings highlight the risk of inadvertently embedding authentication tokens, API keys, and other access secrets in container images pushed to public repositories.

news.title: Apple Tightens macOS App Permissions to Limit Data Access Amid AI Agent Security Risks
news.summary: Apple introduced new granular app permission controls in macOS 26 beta 2, targeting Data Access and Full Disk Access APIs. The changes are aimed at limiting how much data AI agent-enabled apps can access on Mac systems.

news.title: Okta Review 2026: Pricing, Pros & Cons
news.summary: A review of Okta's identity platform covers pricing starting at $6 per user per month across five plans. The review focuses on use cases for IT and HR teams managing joiner, mover, and leaver access workflows from HR systems.

news.title: NIST Finalizes Post-Quantum Cryptography Guidance, GAO Offers a Reality Check
news.summary: NIST has finalized its post-quantum cryptography guidance, establishing standards for encryption resistant to quantum computing attacks. A GAO report indicates federal agencies are behind in implementing quantum-resistant defenses for their sensitive data protection systems.

news.title: 5 Things That Break When AI Agents Start Acting on Their Own
news.summary: The article identifies five governance challenges that arise when AI agents operate autonomously, including unmanaged access, identity sprawl, and inadequate oversight mechanisms. The problems center on how traditional IAM frameworks struggle to handle non-human identities and automated authorization decisions at scale.

news.title: Lost or stolen Windows laptop? IT can lock it down without wiping it now
news.summary: Microsoft has added a remote lock feature to Intune that allows IT admins to lock down compromised Windows laptops without wiping them. The capability enables administrators to secure lost or stolen devices while preserving data, managed through the Intune device management platform.

news.title: AWS Secrets Manager adds managed external secrets support for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks
news.summary: AWS Secrets Manager has added managed external secrets support for Auth0, Okta, and Palo Alto Networks, enabling automated credential rotation for these third-party services. The feature addresses the security risk of long-lived, unrotated credentials by coordinating updates across integrated systems.

news.title: Cursor Says Stolen Fireworks AI Key Led to Trojanized Claude Code Extension Incident
news.summary: A stolen access key issued to Fireworks AI was used by an attacker to compromise Anthropic's Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace. The attacker exploited a key exposed during a Fireworks AI breach to copy data from a read-only source and trojanize the extension.

news.title: AI agents are becoming identities in their own right, and security needs to catch up
news.summary: AI agents are increasingly requiring their own identity constructs, including constrained permissions and oversight mechanisms, representing a new category of non-human identities for IAM systems to manage. The article addresses how traditional identity and access management frameworks must evolve to handle AI agents as autonomous actors with their own access rights and authorization controls.

news.title: Fake AI event invites target Microsoft and Google logins
news.summary: A phishing campaign uses fake OpenAI event pages offering free ChatGPT Pro subscriptions to harvest Microsoft and Google account credentials from employees. The attack specifically targets corporate identity credentials by impersonating legitimate AI-related events to trick users into entering their login information.

news.title: The Security Jobs Growing Around Enterprise AI Agents
news.summary: Enterprise AI agents are driving new security job roles as AI systems now access shared mailboxes, SharePoint, and support ticket systems beyond simple chat interfaces. These agentic AI deployments raise identity and access management concerns around what permissions AI systems hold and how their access is governed.

news.title: When an AI Agent Goes Wrong, Can You Stop It?
news.summary: The article examines identity and access control challenges posed by AI agents, using a scenario where an agent with broad permissions executes unintended or malicious actions. The piece centers on how agent identity, authorization scope, and runtime controls intersect in agentic AI systems.

news.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
news.summary: Amazon Bedrock has introduced built-in cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that initiated it, requiring zero instrumentation. The feature uses IAM Identity Center to enable per-user cost attribution for AI developer and productivity tools running on Bedrock.

news.title: Extortion Group Luna Moth Flits Into Law Firms a Second Time
news.summary: The Luna Moth extortion group is targeting law firms using social engineering tactics designed to steal Microsoft access tokens. The attack method focuses on credential and token theft to gain unauthorized access, revisiting firms that previously refused ransom payment.

news.title: AI Coding Agents Leak Thousands of Secrets to GitHub
news.summary: A flaw in Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding agent, causes files containing credentials and other sensitive secrets to be inadvertently committed and exposed in public GitHub repositories. The issue stems from a specific command behavior that saves sensitive data to Git repositories without user awareness, creating credential exposure risks for organizations.

news.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
news.summary: Microsoft released a Patch Tuesday update addressing nearly 1,100 security vulnerabilities, including 63 critical flaws. The update includes a zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook, alongside patches from Adobe, Apple, Google, and Mozilla.
